tasks.title: Implement capability-based setup for empty and existing projects
tasks.description:
Outcome: Capability-based project setup before or after language selection.

Current implementation: Planning may start in an empty folder with no language. Tool preparation cannot rely on detecting source that does not exist.

Implementation responsibility:
- Start from user discussion and declared stack; later validate against detected source/configuration and mixed repositories.
- Resolve required analysis operations against extensible provider metadata, local compatible tools and explicit project settings.
- Produce a concrete preparation/configuration plan with versions/platform/prerequisites; follow existing authorization before installs or environment changes.
- Validate actual provider results before advertising capability; keep planning/search useful with undecided or unsupported languages.
- Store setup state per project/workspace/configuration through the shared service, independent of Heca.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Empty/non-Git/stack-undecided projects initialize without a language guess.
- No protocol is assumed to discover/install every language tool universally.
- New languages on an existing adapter can be configured through metadata without a core whitelist.

tasks.title: Discover and configure analysis providers through shared adapters
tasks.description:
Outcome: Extensible provider adapters for complementary syntactic, semantic and persistent index capabilities.

Current implementation: SCIP, LSP and syntax parsing solve different problems. TypeScript is the product implementation language, not a Rust/C/Java analyzer.

Implementation responsibility:
- Define versioned provider manifests/catalog entries with language/version selectors, operations, configuration/build prerequisites, preparation and probes.
- Implement common adapter ports for registered compatible SCIP import, live LSP and syntax/text providers selected by the actual stack.
- Report coverage per provider/operation/source area/configuration; no three-tool mandatory installation or invented semantic support.
- Manage provider/index lifecycle outside user application dependencies and pass normalized results/provenance into code links and graph.
- Leave shared live language-server process ownership to T485; do not start a competing editor-specific runtime.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Metadata can register another supported language family without editing a hard-coded core switch.
- Syntax, semantic reference and historical index results expose their real differences.
- Unsupported operations produce explicit coverage gaps and usable fallback.

tasks.title: Verify dynamic provider coverage and mixed-language boundaries
tasks.description:
Outcome: Verified dynamic provider coverage across unrelated languages and mixed source boundaries.

Current implementation: An isolated TypeScript anchor proof does not establish multilingual production support.

Implementation responsibility:
- Create isolated fixtures for several unrelated language families and dynamically added metadata on an existing adapter; named languages are examples, not the supported set.
- Exercise actual selected providers where available and label contract fixtures separately; test configuration/build/platform mismatch and missing tools.
- Verify mixed-language imports/references, generated files, monorepo roots, partial syntax-only areas and unsupported code.
- Ensure capability changes invalidate affected source evidence and do not silently upgrade text/syntax output into semantic confidence.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Each claimed operation has provider/version/configuration/source evidence or a named missing check.
- No mandatory language whitelist or universal TypeScript compiler claim remains.
- Planning/context retrieval works when every semantic provider is unavailable.
